rows.question: This team of dogs pulls a sled with a mass of 60 kilograms. Assume there is no one on the sled. It takes 80 seconds to run 1000 meters along a straight ice surface from rest. Assuming the resistance encountered by the sled during the movement remains unchanged, it is known that the sled will move in a straight line with uniform acceleration within the first 8 seconds of movement. Starting from the end of the 8th second, the power of the dog sled team remains unchanged, causing the sled to continue to move in a straight line. In the last period, the sled will move The dog sledding team is moving in a straight line at a constant speed, with a speed of 15 meters per second. The average power of the dog sled team in the first 8 seconds of movement is half of the power after 8 seconds. Find the average power of the dog sled team during the entire movement and the resistance the sled suffered during the movement.
rows.prediction:
The average power of the dog sled team during the entire movement can be calculated as follows:

Power = Force x Speed

The force exerted by the dog sled team is given as 60 kilograms, which is the mass of the sled. The speed of the sled is 15 meters per second, which is constant throughout the movement.

Power = 60 kg x 15 m/s = 900 kg-m/s

The resistance encountered by the sled during the movement is given as 80 seconds to run 1000 meters along a straight ice surface from rest. This can be converted to a force by dividing the resistance by the sled's mass:

Resistance = Force x Distance

Resistance = 80 s x 1000 m / 60 kg = 13.33 N

The average power of the dog sled team during the entire movement is the total power divided by the time taken:

Average Power = Total Power / Time

Average Power = 900 kg-m/s / 80 s = 11.25 kg-m/s

The resistance encountered by the sled during the movement is 13.33 N.
